A total of 105 isolated teeth were identified as avialan and can be divided into seven distinct morphotypes. Crucially, decades of extensive microfossil sampling have failed to produce any evidence of crocodyliforms in the PCF, allowing us to rule out this possible identity. Further, the teeth described here can be distinguished from those of all non-avialan theropods known in the PCF. Our morphotypes thus provide an important framework for identifying bird teeth in other Late Cretaceous microfossil assemblages as well as understanding avialan diversity before the K–Pg extinction.
n760d688f9262: Hybrid quantum–classical machine learning on noisy intermediate-scale quantum (NISQ) devices suffers from three coupled overheads: hardware miscalibration, classical syndrome-decoding latency and shot noise on gradient estimators. We present quantum calibration and observable processing (QCOP), a unified closed-loop control layer integrating a spectral calibration engine (SCE), a hierarchical syndrome decoder (HSD) and an observable compression layer (OCL) within a single GPU-accelerated pipeline. Three theoretical bounds characterize the joint effect on logical error rate (LER), convergence rate and observable variance. On device-calibrated noise-model simulators (n=20 seeds), QCOP achieves up to 2× wall-clock training speed-up and approximately 40% variational quantum eigensolver (VQE) energy error reduction relative to the unaugmented baseline. A hardware pilot on ibm_nairobi at surface-code distance d=5 (2000 syndrome volumes, 8192 shots each, single calibration window) yields a 1.6× latency reduction and 1.9× LER reduction for the HSD over minimum-weight perfect matching (MWPM)—directionally consistent with simulation but quantitatively smaller, indicating noise sources beyond the model. This pilot exercises the HSD alone: the SCE and the OCL have not been run on physical hardware, and the three modules have never been executed jointly on a device. The end-to-end QCOP benefits—speed-up, energy error reduction and variance reduction—are therefore not hardware-validated, and end-to-end hardware validation of all three modules remains future work. Code and model weights are available at https://github.com/hekimoghlu/QCOP.
nf33364b8015d: The synthesis of monolayer graphene has progressed from exfoliation to bottom-up strategies, enabling increasing atomic-level control. This review compares key routes, chemical vapour deposition (CVD), SiC epitaxy, arc discharge, molecular assembly and single-atom catalysts (SACs) and evaluates their mechanisms, scalability and quality bottlenecks. CVD remains the most mature and scalable approach, delivering centimetre-scale-single-crystal films through optimized substrates, roll-to-roll annealing and dry transfer, yet transfer-induced defects and wafer-scale non-uniformity persist. SiC epitaxy enables transfer-free, wafer-scale graphene with well-aligned domains, but requires high temperatures and costly wafers. Arc discharge offers catalyst-free production of crystalline graphene flakes, although monolayer yield and purity remain limited. Molecular assembly provides unmatched structural programmability and atomic precision in nanoribbons and nanographene islands, typically restricted to micrometre scales and stringent conditions. SAC-mediated growth represents a precision limit, where isolated metal atoms catalyse single-carbon insertion or removal at graphene edges, though current demonstrations remain largely single-event observations. Complementing these routes, artificial intelligence/machine learning is increasingly used for parameter optimization, predictive modelling of domain size/uniformity/defects and automated quality control (convolutional neural network/ generative modelling and YOLO-based defect detection). Overall, industrially viable, defect-free monolayer graphene will require combining scalable growth, transfer-free integration, atomic-precision and AI-enabled closed-loop optimization.
na1ff310586e8: Generative agents powered by large language models (LLMs) demonstrate human-like characteristics through sophisticated natural language interactions. Their ability to assume roles and personalities based on predefined character biographies has positioned them as cost-effective substitutes for human participants in social science research. This paper explores the validity of such persona-based agents1 in representing human populations; we recreate the HEXACO personality inventory experiment by surveying 310 GPT-4 powered agents, conducting factor analysis on their responses, and comparing these results to the original findings presented by Ashton et al. (Ashton et al. 2004 J. Pers. Soc. Psychol. 87, 707–721 (doi:10.1037/0022-3514.87.5.707). Our results found (i) a coherent and reliable personality structure was recoverable from the agents’ responses demonstrating partial alignment to the HEXACO framework, (ii) the derived personality dimensions were consistent and reliable within GPT-4, when coupled with a sufficiently curated population, and (iii) cross-model analysis revealed variability in personality profiling, suggesting model-specific biases and limitations. We discuss the practical considerations and challenges encountered during the experiment. This study contributes to the ongoing discourse on the potential benefits and limitations of using generative agents in social science research and provides useful guidance on designing consistent and representative agent personas to maximize coverage and representation of human personality traits, while highlighting potential limitations of applying human psychometric frameworks to generative agents.
neb1570ec24da: Loot boxes are randomized rewards in video games. Meta-analyses suggest relationships between loot box spending and problem gambling symptomatology, and early longitudinal evidence suggests loot box purchasers migrate into conventional gambling at higher rates than non-purchasers. Regulatory responses vary across jurisdictions, and even in jurisdictions that have banned loot boxes, evidence suggests their presence in games remains common. Consequently, consumers are often responsible for regulating their own, and their children’s, loot box purchasing. To effectively achieve this, consumers must first be able to identify loot boxes. Here, we investigated consumer accuracy in identifying critical features of loot boxes. Participants were tasked to identify basic facts about, pictures of, and receipts generated by loot boxes. Parents and non-gamers, compared with non-parents and gamers, respectively, were poorer at identifying loot boxes. Our results suggest that parents and non-gamers may be less equipped to make informed loot box purchasing decisions compared with non-parents/non-guardians and gamers, respectively. This may pose risks for parents and unaware incipient gamers. These are the first findings providing objective evidence about the relative ability of consumers to identify, and thus self-regulate purchases of, loot boxes and suggest that parents and non-gamers may require support to ensure informed purchasing decisions.
n05c6c4984c30: In human language, word order impacts how words are categorized and understood (as nouns, verbs etc.). We have demonstrated that this effect extends to non-linguistic stimuli, suggesting that the impact of sequence order on stimulus categorization is a domain-general, rather than language-specific cognitive process. Here, we ask if this process is evolutionarily conserved in other non-human primates. We developed a non-linguistic experiment and tested rhesus macaques (Macaca mulatta) and bonobos (Pan paniscus). Participants first learned to categorize shapes (as rounded, squared or pointed). We next assessed how they categorized ambiguous morph shapes by combining exemplars from each category. We provided sequential information by training the animals to select shapes in a specified order: rounded, then squared and then pointed. Finally, we assessed whether presentation in specific positions in this learned sequence would impact subsequent categorization of ambiguous morph shapes. In humans, an ambiguous morph was more likely to be categorized as the shape it replaced in a sequence. Non-human primates, however, showed no such effect, categorizing stimuli independent of their position in a sequence. This suggests that the tendency to infer category membership from sequence order is not shared across primates, and may have evolved more recently in the human lineage.
nbd05594d8f94: Mirror life presents a low-likelihood but high-severity global biosecurity threat that has attracted the attention of bioscientists, governments and international security organizations. However, current analytical techniques are not fit to identify mirror life biohazards. Herein, we propose the first assay method for screening against mirror life. This approach is based upon optical circularly polarized luminesce (CPL) signatures generated by fluorescent probes, which bind to subcellular targets (e.g. membranes, organelles, nucleic acids, etc.). Probes can either be achiral or be intrinsically chiral. We set out why a multi-probe reporter panel approach incorporating many CPL-generating probes is necessary to identify mirror life with a high degree of confidence (i.e. avoiding false positives). The distinct CPL signatures can be analysed via recent innovations in CPL detection, i.e. rapid CPL spectroscopy, CPL microscopy (enantioselective differential chiral contrast, EDCC, imaging) and CPL EDCC cameras. While these are advanced technologies, they share the same fundamental optical principles as three-dimensional cinema glasses and so are amenable to scaling and portable applications. The CPL assay approach to mirror life screening could be a useful tool for screening against mirror life biohazards and ensuring compliance with any potential future international legislation against mirror-life research.
ne6f5460adcac: We propose an iterative programmatic planning (IPP) framework that solves grid-based tasks by using large language models (LLMs) to synthesize interpretable, executable programs that act as agent policies mapping environment states to action sequences, rather than relying on traditional search or reinforcement learning. Alongside prompting strategies such as direct code generation, pseudocode conditioned refinement and curriculum-based prompting, IPP centres on an iterative refinement mechanism that updates code from coarse, task-level feedback. We evaluate our approach using six leading LLMs and two challenging grid-based benchmarks (grid-based reasoning for assessing spatial planning (GRASP) and MiniGrid). Our IPP framework demonstrates improvements over direct code generation for five of the six models, with net energy gains ranging from a few per cent to roughly threefold and, for Gemini-2.5-Pro, a sign flip from a negative baseline to a strongly positive score, establishes a new state-of-the-art result for GRASP and significantly outperforms direct elicitation from GPT-o3-mini (by 43% on the hardest MiniGrid task to 116% on GRASP). While code generation has a higher initial prompting cost compared to direct solution elicitation ($0.08 per task versus $0.002 per instance for GPT-o3-mini), the code can be reused for any number of instances, making the amortized cost significantly lower (by 400 times on GPT-o3-mini across the complete GRASP benchmark). Beyond performance gains, IPP produces reusable, human-readable policies that support transparent inspection and modification, underscoring the advantages of planning as program synthesis over per-instance inference. The code and results can be found at http://github.com/Mystic-Slice/LLM-Planning-CodeGen.
n3476bd0108c4: The Neogene fossil record of Patagonia provides important insights into the evolution and ecological diversification of marine predators in the Southern Hemisphere. Among these, Kawas benegasorum, an extinct seal from the Late Miocene Puerto Madryn Formation, represents the only record of a putative phocine (northern seals) in the Southern Hemisphere and preserves rare evidence of stomach contents. However, its original description was concise, and lacked detailed information on its dentition and stomach contents, leaving aspects of its morphology, phylogeny and paleoecology unresolved. We re-describe the holotype and only known specimen of K. benegasorum, providing the first comprehensive study of its postcranial morphology, new information on its dentition and a detailed examination of its stomach contents. We show that Kawas has both monachine- and phocine-like traits, with an overall morphology suggesting affinities with Monachinae. However, phylogenetic analyses yielded conflicting results, recovering Kawas either within Phocinae or in an unresolved position within Phocidae. The stomach contents indicate a piscivorous diet with coastal, benthic and demersal prey, broadly comparable to that of extant South American sea lions inhabiting the region. These results document early benthic nearshore foraging in pinnipeds and suggest dietary convergence across geological time in the western South Atlantic by the Late Miocene.
n3489e2461cca: Several species rely on mechanisms to resolve conflicts and reduce their negative consequences, including reconciliation and third-party affiliation (i.e. post-conflict affiliative interactions between victims and aggressors, and between victims and third parties, respectively). Here, we studied reconciliation and third-party affiliation in two groups of wolves (n = 20) and three groups of wolves introgressed with dogs (i.e. second- or later-generation backcrosses of wolf-dog hybrids to wolves; n = 13), in captivity. We conducted behavioural observations of post-conflict affiliative interactions using continuous focal sampling for 2 minutes following an aggression, and during matched-control periods. Our results showed that both admixed and non-admixed wolves engaged in post-conflict affiliation consistent with reconciliation and third-party affiliation. Although we found no evidence that admixed wolves showed lower reconciliation or third-party affiliation than non-admixed wolves, social factors had different modulatory effects in admixed and non-admixed wolves. In particular, stronger social bonds promoted post-conflict affiliation in non-admixed wolves, whereas greater rank distance was associated with higher post-conflict affiliation in admixed wolves. Moreover, post-conflict affiliation was more likely following high-intensity aggression in both admixed and non-admixed wolves, and after unidirectional conflicts in the latter. These findings indicate that dog introgression may influence post-conflict behaviour in wolves and suggest that, while both admixed and non-admixed wolves engage in post-conflict affiliation, the mechanisms underlying them may partially differ.
n278be3486cb3: Pathogens exert strong selective pressure on group-living primates. In humans, disease defence includes both a biological and behavioural immune system, which includes the emotion of disgust and avoidance behaviours shaped by genetics, learning and culture. While pathogen avoidance is documented in nonhuman primates, little is known about how ecological and developmental factors influence pathogen sensitivity, that is, individual variation in pathogen avoidance. We conducted two studies to examine this in macaques. Our first study tested macaques (n = 54) from seven different species and four different rearing backgrounds in a visual food-choice task where food was either placed on a substrate with or without pathogenic cues. Macaques preferred feeding on non-contaminated substrates, with sanctuary-born individuals showing greater avoidance than former pets. Our second study tested sanctuary-born Japanese macaques (n = 55) from four groups; three groups had recently experienced an infectious disease outbreak. Macaques from exposed groups showed significantly higher avoidance of contaminated substrates. Together, our findings suggest that early life rearing experience and recent disease exposure shape pathogen sensitivity in macaques, demonstrating a flexible behavioural immune system in Old World monkeys. These findings suggest that flexible, context-sensitive pathogen avoidance is present in Old World monkeys, providing the behavioural foundations from which human disgust may have evolved.
n5cc5b50de041: Planning is critical for adaptive behaviour in a changing world, because it lets us anticipate the future and adjust our actions accordingly. While prefrontal cortex is crucial for this process, it remains unknown how planning is implemented in neural circuits. Prefrontal representations were recently discovered in simpler sequence memory tasks, where different populations of neurons represent different future time points. We demonstrate that combining such representations with the ubiquitous principle of neural attractor dynamics allows circuits to solve much richer problems, including planning. This is achieved by embedding the environment structure directly in synaptic connections to implement an attractor network that infers desirable futures. The resulting ‘spacetime attractor’ excels at planning in challenging tasks known to depend on the prefrontal cortex. Recurrent neural networks trained by gradient descent on such tasks learn a solution that precisely recapitulates the spacetime attractor – in representation, in dynamics, and in connectivity. Analyses of networks trained across different environment structures reveal a generalisation mechanism that rapidly reconfigures the world model used for planning, without the need for synaptic plasticity. The spacetime attractor is a testable mechanistic theory of planning. If true, it would provide a path towards detailed mechanistic understanding of how prefrontal cortex structures adaptive behaviour.
n92841ace8bd1: Adaptive behavior requires assigning emotional value to sensory cues and generalizing to similar stimuli. The prelimbic cortex (PL) is critical for threat expression and discrimination, yet its neuronal ensembles undergo substantial turnover over time. How stable population codes emerge despite this reorganization remains unknown. Using longitudinal calcium imaging in freely moving mice, we tracked PL activity for 30 days during auditory discriminative fear learning and retrieval. Despite substantial ensemble turnover, stable graded representations persisted in PL populations. A generalized linear model showed that the tone threat value explained graded activity better than freezing, indicating that PL primarily encodes stimulus significance. Population similarity across stimulus presentations was highest for shock-associated and highly generalized tones, suggesting a stable population code underlying threat generalization. Stable neurons preserved graded gradients across sessions, whereas learning modulated the rate of dynamic frequency-selective neurons. Together, these populations enabled stable threat-value coding despite ongoing ensemble reorganization.
nfd8d863c3b3b: Endosymbiotic bacteria can affect many ecological attributes of their insect hosts, including (in herbivorous insects) how they interact with plants where they feed. This raises the issue of whether deliberate endosymbiont introductions could be used to decrease crop damage caused by insect pests. Here, we investigate how transinfecting Rickettsiella viridis and Regiella insecticola endosymbionts into a novel pest aphid host, the Russian wheat aphid (Diuraphis noxia), influences population growth, alate production, dispersal ability, and crop damage. Both the Rickettsiella (originating from pea aphids) and Regiella (from green peach aphids) were stably maintained in their new host where they had contrasting effects. Rickettsiella increased the severity of aphid feeding damage on wheat and barley, resulting in greater leaf loss, chlorotic streaking, and higher aphid populations, whereas Regiella reduced aphid population growth and the severity of feeding damage by aphids. Their effects on dispersal morphology also differed: Regiella had no detectable impact on alate incidence, while Rickettsiella consistently suppressed wing formation in small cages, and in larger mesocosms with multiple wheat plants this endosymbiont suppressed dispersal. nd29d584f049f: Prison work has become a focus of research in corrections, with studies examining deleterious effects of nearly every aspect of the occupation.
